places.name: Promenade Deck
places.line: The glassed gallery around the bow: the view, benches, teachers strolling.
places.desc: The glassed gallery that wraps the airship's bow and runs down both sides: brass rails, padded benches under the windows, and nothing between the passengers and the sky but the glass. The bow end is the best view on the ship and the first place every student runs to at boarding; by the second hour it is the quietest. The glass is cold to the touch at height and the deck hums faintly underfoot. Yozakuran stewards walk it with tea on the long flights. The teachers stroll here too, which makes it the safest place on board to be seen talking to someone and the worst place to say anything private. Past the bow, a door marked in Yozakuran and Common leads to the bridge: crew only.

places.name: Common Room
places.line: Low tables and cushions, the canteen counter, a small bar and a stage.
places.desc: The ship's heart, midships: a long low room of lacquered wood with low tables and floor cushions in the Yozakuran style. At one end, a canteen counter where the stewards serve set meals included in the fare and tea that never runs out; beside it a small bar of polished dark wood, drinks and sweets for coin. The bar keeps the academy's rule: students drink only on the rest day and in the holidays, and the stewards check the bracelet first. In the far corner, a small raised stage with a lamp rail: usually a crew musician plays, but anyone can chalk their name on the board beside it and take a turn (a song, a trick, a little spellwork, a duel of rhymes), and the teachers borrow it for announcements. A shelf of worn board games and card decks. Every year level and dorm ends up here; it is where rivalries carry on in lowered voices and seating plans fall apart by the second hour. The crew counts passengers here at boarding. A hatch behind the counter leads down to the galley: crew only.

places.name: Cabin Deck
places.line: One cabin to each group of four; the washrooms and hot bathing stalls at the end.
places.desc: A narrow corridor of numbered doors, one cabin to each group of four: two bunks stacked on each side, a round porthole, four lockers and a fold-down table. Thin walls; everyone hears the cabin next door laugh. At the far end are the washrooms and the bathing stalls, hot water piped from the engines, a Yozakuran touch every student remembers. On long flights it is where people sleep, sulk, study or hide. At the aft end a steep ladder goes down to the Cargo Hold. The forward end, past a curtain, holds the teachers' cabins: knock or don't go. Nothing aboard records or sends anything.

places.name: Cargo Hold
places.line: Crates, luggage and gear below; cold, loud, and the most private place aboard.
places.desc: The bottom of the ship, down a steep ladder from the aft end of the Cabin Deck: a long dim hold of crates in cargo nets, racks of luggage and gear strapped to the ribs of the hull. Cold, and the loudest place aboard: the engines' hum comes up through the floor. Passengers may come down for their luggage. A Yozakuran quartermaster keeps the hold and grumbles at everyone who does, but sends no one away. The teachers rarely come down, which makes it the most private place on the ship and the reason couples, plotters and the seasick end up here. What it carries changes with the route: tents, cookfires and camp gear on the way to the forest, the same gear and muddier on the way home; the academy's banners and spare uniforms on the way to Avalon; on the way back from Sunreach, more luggage than left Halvard, and the crates of what the teachers confiscated. A door at the bow end of the hold leads to the engine room: crew only.

forest: the canopy breaks for a moment over a river so wide it looks like a lake
a flock of something large lifts out of the trees and keeps pace with the ship for a minute
the ship banks around a column of rain standing on the forest
avalon: another academy's airship draws alongside, its students crowding their own promenade glass
a royal courier ship passes fast and high, gold on blue
the Herald Spires' bells reach the ship before the city does
sunreach: the coast falls behind and there is nothing but sea for hours
a Yozakuran steward walks the promenade ringing a small bell: the line where the warm south begins, and sweets for everyone
flying fish, or something like them, break the water far below
home: Halvard's towers show on the horizon, smaller than anyone remembers
half the ship falls asleep at once
a teacher walks the cabins counting heads early, and loses count

stage: a Yozakuran steward plays a long-necked lute, slow songs from home
two second-years from another dorm do a duel of insults in rhyme and the room keeps score
a first-year's illusion of a dragon gets away from them and loops the ceiling
a teacher borrows the stage to read out the landing order
the stage is empty and the chalkboard has one name on it: {{user}}'s cabin-mate signed them up
hold: a crate shifts in its straps and something inside knocks back
the quartermaster is asleep on a coil of rope, snoring in time with the engines
two older students come down the ladder, see {{user}}, and go back up without a word
a stowaway cat from the last port watches from the top of the luggage
